title: Pompey the Great
objective: After this level you can describe Pompey’s rise and his conquests in the East.
summary: Pompey rose under Sulla, won huge commands, swept the pirates from the sea in 67 BCE and remade the East. He was hailed as Magnus, “the Great.”

cards.headline: His soldiers hailed him as “the Great,” and he made the name his own.
cards.body: Signing yourself “the Great” takes confidence. Pompey had it, and a string of victories to back it up. Here’s how he earned a name borrowed from Alexander.

cards.headline: A general of special commands
cards.body: Pompey first rose to fame as a young commander fighting for Sulla. Then the Roman people voted him extraordinary commands, giving one man power over huge areas for years at a time. Compare that with a consul: one year in office, and a colleague who could block him. Pompey got whole regions, for years. That’s not a job. That’s a kingdom on loan.

cards.headline: Remaking the East
cards.body: Pompey defeated King Mithridates and reorganized the eastern Mediterranean. He made Syria a Roman province and captured Jerusalem in 63 BCE. By then he already had a name to match. His troops, and Sulla too, had hailed him as Magnus, “the Great,” and Pompey used it. It echoed Alexander the Great, whom he admired and imitated. Pompey wasn’t aiming low.

cards.fact: Pompey swept the pirates from the Mediterranean in about three months.
cards.context: Three months to clear a whole sea. The campaign of 67 BCE was one of the extraordinary commands the Roman people voted him, and it shows why those commands were so powerful: one man, a huge area, and the time to finish the job.

questions.prompt: What name did Pompey carry, echoing Alexander?

options.label: Augustus, “the revered one”
options.rationale: That came later, with someone else.

questions.explanation: His troops and Sulla hailed Pompey as Magnus, a name that echoed Alexander the Great.

questions.prompt: Why did Pompey’s commands worry many senators?

options.label: They gave one man vast power for years
They cost Rome its eastern provinces
They were won by bribing the Vestals
They put Carthage back in power

questions.explanation: Extraordinary commands concentrated power in one man, the very thing the Republic was built to prevent.
